title: Live proof: a small real PRD from repository to release, surviving a forced crash mid-write
description:
Filed by architect-16a01670 from parent task-e7a3d643bde34da7b27495dbda745739 (epic breakdown, human-directed 2026-09-04). EPIC-FINAL integration-and-hardening row (get_context.isEpicFinal); the ONLY row of this epic that carries dependsOn - the owner chose this explicitly on 2026-09-04 as the single exception to 'tasks should be full and not depended on other tasks', so the runtime withholds it until every feature row is DONE.

VISION 'Next major milestone': 'Give Moe a small but real PRD. Moe asks the necessary questions, creates the architecture and UX, builds the complete application, launches a working preview, proves every requirement, survives a forced crash, and prepares a production-ready release.' Stage 1 bar (proposed, 2026-08-22): the crash lands MID-WRITE and recovery is provable from durable records alone, never from agent memory.

DELIVERABLE: run the whole loop on a FRESH product from the browser only, with real seats, and record it: New product from PRD (bootstrapped repository) -> Activate project -> Gate 1 with at least one real clarification -> Design -> plan -> nodes built in parallel to 100% criteria coverage -> working preview approved (Gate 2) -> release PR opened with the dossier (Gate 3) -> PREVIEW environment deployed with migrations and environment variables -> health probes UP. During one node's landing, kill the daemon process mid-write (a fault-injection knob the daemon already carries or this row adds under a DEVELOPMENT_ONLY flag), restart it, and prove recovery from the store alone: the landing is either COMMITTED exactly once or REFUSED with a code - never duplicated, never lost. Every criterion in the dossier is VERIFIED at the released sha.

ALSO OWNS (rails: the verification budget concentrates in the epic-final row): the whole-epic regression across every lane including the per-package apps/** runs; the docs sweep (README 'What runs today' and 'What this is not' rewritten to the measured state with its date, VISION roadmap status lines, runbook covering every new kind); the adversarial pass over the epic's new human-only kinds (each MCP-excluded, each refusal code reachable); and the follow-up items the feature rows recorded in their comments.

THE PRD: small but real - e.g. a 3-screen TypeScript web app with sign-in, one PostgreSQL table and one API; the human supplies or approves it at claim time (comment on this row). Dogfood note: Moe shipping its own pull request on moe-next remains the harder dogfood (VISION); this row's proof is the fresh product, not moe-next itself.
definitionOfDone: Transcript of the full browser-only run on a fresh product recorded as a row comment series (each under 4500 chars): bootstrap receipt, activation witness, Gate 1 decision id + the clarification, design ref, plan run id, node landing shas (at least 2 nodes, at least 2 staffed concurrently), preview receipt + decision, release receipt + PR URL, deploy receipt + health URL, migration receipt, environment fingerprints.

Forced crash mid-write: the daemon is killed during a landing write (knob name + timestamp recorded); after restart the ledger shows exactly one outcome for that landing (COMMITTED once or REFUSED with its code) and the goal resumes; the recovery evidence is a store query quoted with its result, not a log line.
The release dossier at the released sha shows every approved criterion VERIFIED (n/n) and is attached to the opened PR (URL in the comment).

Whole-epic regression green with count lines quoted: `pnpm test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`, `pnpm test:integration` (from PowerShell), `pnpm test:security`, `pnpm test:property`.
README 'What runs today' + 'What this is not' rewritten to the measured 'as of <date>' state; VISION Stage 1 / Stage 2 status lines updated; the runbook covers every kind this epic added.

Adversarial pass comment: a table of every human-only kind added by this epic -> its MCP refusal code -> the test file:line that pins it; every follow-up item recorded in the feature rows' comments is either closed here or listed with a reason.
taskRails: FEATURES ONLY (human DoD 2026-09-04): no security-boundary or policy work in this row. The verifier stays the documented trusted-workspace v0.1 limitation; signing, hermetic verification and freeze manifests are out of scope.

EVIDENCE, NEVER FABRICATION (epic rail 4 + global rails): every claim in the transcript names its measurement anchor (store path, sha, receipt id); a gate that prints no count line did not run; a live step that refuses is recorded verbatim and the row goes BLOCKED with blockedOnTaskIds or a comment - never a narrowed DoD.

PROVE IT LIVE: the run is a fresh product directory (not UnAI's existing store) driven from the browser only; the seeds/scripts under scratchpad are not used for any step the product claims to do itself. Never restart the wrapper to unstick a seat (claim TTL 30 min, memory real-seat-cannot-release-its-claim-2026-09-04).

implementationPlan.description: THE FAULT-INJECTION KNOB — the one piece of PRODUCTION code this row writes, and it does not exist yet. MEASURED at plan time: `grep -rn 'FAULT_INJECT|DEVELOPMENT_ONLY|MOE_CRASH|crashAfter|killAfter' --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src` returns ZERO, so the description's 'a knob the daemon already carries or this row adds' resolves to ADDS. Add it under an explicit DEVELOPMENT_ONLY flag that is OFF by default and refuses to arm when the daemon is not in development mode — a crash knob reachable in a normal run is a denial-of-service switch, and this row's rail 1 keeps security work out of scope precisely so the knob must not become one. It kills the daemon at a NAMED point during a landing write. REUSE THE EXISTING CRASH MACHINERY FIRST: tests/e2e/foundation/j3-crash-harness.ts and j3-crash-recovery.e2e.test.ts already kill and restart a real daemon and assert recovery, and dispatch-crash-sweep.e2e.test.ts sweeps dispatch crashes — read them before inventing a mechanism, and say in the step note whether the knob is new or an extension of theirs.
implementationPlan.note:
THE KNOB IS UNCHANGED FROM ROUND 1 AND IS NOW ARMED IN A REAL DRIVE. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/landing-fault-injection.ts` shipped in round 1: OFF unless `MOE_FAULT_INJECT_LANDING` names a point, REFUSES unless `MOE_DEVELOPMENT_ONLY` is exactly "1", four named points, three stable refusal codes (FAULT_INJECTION_DISARMED / _NOT_DEVELOPMENT / _POINT_UNKNOWN). It is an EXTENSION of the existing crash machinery in spirit but a new mechanism: j3-crash-harness kills a daemon from OUTSIDE, this knob kills the landing pass from INSIDE at a named point, which is the only way to hit the window between the git effect and the completion that records it. No production line changed this round.

WHAT THIS ROUND ADDS, all of it under tests/: three modules that close the rejection's three clauses, plus the wiring.

1. REAL PROVIDER SEATS (clause 2). `tests/e2e/control-room/live-proof-seat.ts` writes a LAUNCHER the wrapper spawns through its own `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND` seam. The launcher reads the mission on stdin, matches production's own claim clause (`landingSeatClaim`), marks its window, and spawns a REAL `claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions` with cwd = the product workspace. It contains no product code: the only outcome it can manufacture is `SEAT_PROVIDER_WROTE_NOTHING`, which is a FAILURE. The instruction it adds to the mission names CONSTRAINTS only (one file, .mjs, run the checks, touch nothing else) and never an export name, a code or a signature - those exist only in the acceptance checks, which come from the browser-approved contract.
   `live-proof-workspace.ts` lost its `NODE_MODULES` table and its `liveSeatDouble` entirely; what remains is a roster (`NODE_KEYS`) and `checksFor`. The header sentence QA cited - "The seat is the ONE double" - is gone, replaced by a statement of what happened and why.

   MEASURED, not assumed. I smoke-ran the launcher against a real workspace before touching the drive: mission in, `claude` spawned, module out in 36 s, 3325 bytes, and all three of node-auth-api's committed checks answered `crit-a1 VERIFIED` / `crit-a2 VERIFIED` / `crit-a3 VERIFIED`. The provider chose SHA-256 + `timingSafeEqual` with a dummy digest for unknown users - a thing no line of mine suggested, which is the point. `providerStatus: 0`, `agent: "claude"` in the seat's own end mark.

2. THE OPERATOR LEGS (clause 1). `live-proof-deploy.ts` (target, environment variables + their fingerprints, the deploy, and a two-way health probe), `live-proof-migration.ts` (a real `postgres:16-alpine`, a real `pg_dump` BEFORE the DDL, the receipt written by the SHIPPED `recordMigrationReceipt`, and the constraint name read back from `pg_constraint` rather than from the DDL I sent), `live-proof-image.ts` (the product's deployable surface), `live-proof-operate.ts` (the ordered pass). Every dispatch rides the CONFIGURED OPERATOR wire per comment-267eccae item 3 and carries `actor: "CONFIGURED_OPERATOR"` in the record. NO FENCE IS TOUCHED.
   Preview and deploy are SEPARATE calls because the product forces it: `deployment.deploy`'s prerequisite table reads a COMMITTED `repository.publish` DECISION, so deploy must follow Gate 3, and Gate 2 precedes Gate 3.
   THE DOCKERFILE IS THE LANE'S AND THE RECORD SAYS SO. Production DOES carry `planDeploymentInfrastructure`, but `grep -rn "planDeploymentInfrastructure" --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src | grep -v test` returns ZERO callers - it is wired to no command kind - and its template targets a pnpm workspace with `packages/api` compiling to `dist/server.js`, which a bootstrapped repository does not have. So the product cannot generate it. Every constant in the lane's version is IMPORTED from the production template module so the shape cannot drift. Recorded as a follow-up, not papered over.

3. THE CRASH IN THE REAL DRIVE (clause 3). `landLiveProofNodes` takes an optional fault and starts the wrapper ARMED; after the first node's round it waits for the knob's own note on fd 2, records it with its pid and timestamp, kills the pass, and restarts a NEW pass with NO arming. `live-proof-recovery.ts` then reads the store three ways with quotable SQL.
   THE POINT IS `before-intent`, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT. `repositoryLandingMayRetry` (repository-landing-attempt.ts:9-13) admits a retry only when the attempt journal reads NO_EFFECT; `after-intent` leaves STARTED and `after-commit` leaves a completion gap, so BOTH resolve to REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_REQUIRED by design - one outcome, never duplicated, deliberately NOT auto-resumed. Those two are already proved in the fault lane. `before-intent` is the point at which RESUMPTION is the product's designed answer, which is what clause 3 asks to see.

TYPECHECK: `tests/**` is in NO tsconfig (`pnpm typecheck` is `pnpm --recursive typecheck` and no package includes tests/), so Playwright's esbuild transform never typechecks these. I ran tsc explicitly over all eight live-proof modules and the spec with --strict --exactOptionalPropertyTypes: ZERO errors

WHAT CLOSED THE THREE REJECTION CLAUSES, each by a measurement rather than by a re-argument:

1. REAL SEATS (clause 2). Unchanged from the previous session's fix and now DRIVEN: three real `claude` seats wrote the three node modules, 68.6s / 69.2s / 80.7s, three distinct landing shas. The seat double and its `NODE_MODULES` table are gone from the lane.

2. THE RECEIPT CHAIN PAST THE PULL REQUEST (clause 1). Preview receipt + ACCEPTED decision, release receipt + PR #5, deploy receipt DEPLOYED with a health URL answering 200, migration receipt APPLIED, and both environment fingerprints. Two production shapes had to be understood first, and both are recorded rather than worked around: (a) `deployment.deploy` is an UPDATE to a RUNNING environment — it discovers a compose-labelled `proxy` on the target network and flips its Caddyfile upstream — so the operator brings the environment up with `docker compose` first, using the production template's own Caddyfile bytes (new `live-proof-environment.ts`); (b) the deploy runs the PRODUCT'S OWN migration keyed by the deploy decision, so the lane's own `applyLiveMigration` collided with it (`MIGRATION_RECEIPT_CONFLICT@DAEMON_INGRESS`) and was replaced by a READ of the product's receipt plus three independent database witnesses (`live-proof-migration.ts` rewritten).

3. THE GOAL RESUMES (clause 3). The knob is armed INSIDE this drive at `after-completion` and the recovery is the product's own `repository.recover`, taken BY CLICK in the browser on the shipped `RepositoryRecoveryCard` — it is human-only by construction, so no seat could have taken it. Exactly one landing outcome for the crashed node (its `landing_receipt`, 1.46s after the crash instant, written by the reconcile), no doubled row anywhere in the landing journal, and both remaining nodes landed after the crash.

THE CRASH POINT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A PREFERENCE, and the three rejected points are named with the source that rejects them: `before-intent` (no durable evidence -> EVIDENCE_MISSING; driven live 20:55:00Z and twenty minutes of a restarted wrapper produced no landing), `after-intent` (attempt STARTED, no commit), `after-commit` (Git committed, nothing journaling it -> CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN by design). Only `after-completion` has a recovery to prove.

FOUR OTHER DEFECTS THIS DRIVE FOUND AND FIXED, all in the lane, none in production:
- the browser recovery loop remounted every 2s and never let `useEffectRead` finish, so it reported RESERVATION_NEVER_OFFERED against a daemon that was offering RECONCILE_LANDED at that instant. It now waits for the read to answer.
- success is read as the reservation NO LONGER BEING OFFERED on a fresh mount, because the confirmation sentence unmounts with the row the refresh removes.
- `concurrentStaffing` read only the LIVE pass's transcript, so an armed run lost the BUSY witness with the pass the crash killed. It now reads every pass.
- the one-outcome count was taken on the NODE ref, which carries no landing decision at all; it is now taken on `landing:<nodeRef>`, where `landingAggregateId` puts them.

TYPECHECK: `npx tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json --noEmit` exit 0 (tests/** is in no package tsconfig, so `pnpm typecheck` never reaches these files).

PEER DIRT, untouched and never a stop condition: apps/daemon/src/repository/migrations/*, controlled-profile-generator.test.ts, preview-goal-landing.test.ts, git-source-extract.*.

implementationPlan.description: THE CRASH, MID-WRITE (DoD 2 — the Stage 1 bar, and the hardest claim in this row). Kill the daemon DURING a landing write, recording the knob name and the timestamp. Then restart and prove recovery FROM THE STORE ALONE, never from agent memory or a log line: the ledger shows EXACTLY ONE outcome for that landing — COMMITTED once, or REFUSED with its code — never duplicated and never lost, and the goal resumes. THE EVIDENCE IS A STORE QUERY QUOTED WITH ITS RESULT (DoD 2 says so explicitly); a log line saying 'recovered' is not evidence, because the log is written by the process whose correctness is in question. Assert the ONE-OUTCOME property by counting rows for that landing in the durable ledger, not by observing that the goal looks fine afterwards — a duplicate landing also looks fine.
implementationPlan.note:
DoD 2 IS PROVED INSIDE THE LIVE DRIVE, BOTH HALVES, FROM THE STORE. Full evidence in comment-0383a78a; this note records the shape and the reasoning.

THE KILL: `MOE_FAULT_INJECT_LANDING point=after-completion pid=36172 at=2026-09-09T22:15:21.038Z`, written by the dying process itself with a synchronous `writeSync(2, …)` before `process.kill(pid, "SIGKILL")`. Not a graceful exit: recovering from a clean shutdown proves nothing.

THE ONE-OUTCOME PROPERTY, counted from ROWS in `command_decisions`:
- crashed node's landing aggregate `landing:node:v1:b474d4d5…` carries exactly TWO decisions: `internal.repository.landing_baseline` (22:14:06.306Z, before the crash) and `internal.repository.landing_receipt` (22:15:22.498Z, after it). ONE landing outcome. The assertion is `crashedNodeLandings === 1` over kinds ending `landing_receipt`.
- the whole landing journal, grouped: three `repository-landing:` aggregates with one `landing_intent` and one `landing_completion` each, three `repository-landing-attempt:` aggregates with one `landing_attempt` each. Every row reads `decisions 1`; the drive asserts the set of rows with `decisions !== 1` is EMPTY.

A DUPLICATE WOULD HAVE BEEN VISIBLE AND WAS POSSIBLE. The restarted wrapper BLOCKS the reservation rather than re-landing (`repository-delivery-coordinator.ts:180`), and the reconcile writes a receipt only when the durable evidence proves Git committed and no receipt exists (`needsLandingReceipt`). Had either guard been wrong, a second `landing_receipt` on that aggregate is exactly what this count catches.

"AND THE GOAL RESUMES", anchored to the crash instant rather than to when the assertion ran: `landing:node:v1:21d65433…` baseline 22:15:23.687Z + receipt 22:16:34.469Z, `landing:node:v1:1e2a9d95…` baseline 22:16:35.142Z + receipt 22:18:11.751Z — all strictly after 22:15:21.038Z, 210 decisions in total after it, and the goal ran on to its completion node, its criteria, its preview and its release.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT CHANGED THE QUERY, and it is the reason the round-1 version of this clause could never have passed: landing outcomes are NOT committed on the node's own ref. `landingAggregateId` (landing-receipt-contracts.ts:137) puts them on `landing:<nodeRef>`; the node ref carries `review.submit`, `internal.integration.verifier_receipt` and `integration.accept_output` and no landing decision at all. A count on the node ref answers ZERO for every node ever landed — a query that cannot fail for the right reason.

WHY THE RECOVERY IS A BROWSER CLICK AND NOT A RE-DRIVEN ROUND: `repository.recover` requires a durable HUMAN principal with `project.admin` and refuses MCP, wrapper and verifier transports, so it is not dispatchable by any agent seat. The card offered `RECONCILE_LANDED` and refused `ABORT_UNEXECUTED` with `REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN` — both directions visible, and the refused one is refused with its code.

The three crash points this drive does NOT use are pinned in the fault lane and their production reasons are quoted in the spec's own source at the arming site.

A dossier that enumerated seven would satisfy "all verified" and fail all three of these.

THE RELEASED SHA IS THE COMPLETION NODE'S OWN LANDING, so "at the released sha" is not a label: `integratedSha` from the criterion evidence, the publish receipt's sha, the release receipt's sha, the dossier header's sha and the deploy receipt's sha are all `d30f9094a931d4789bcbf50996748b1c3e4c741e`, and that is the third landing commit in the product's repository.

implementationPlan.description: WHOLE-EPIC REGRESSION (DoD 4). Every leg standalone and foreground, each `Test Files N passed` count line quoted VERBATIM; a leg that prints no count line DID NOT RUN and must not be reported as a pass (global rail 8, and task rail 2 repeats it). The DoD names: `pnpm test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`, `pnpm test:integration` (from PowerShell), `pnpm test:security`, `pnpm test:property`. === BEGIN PRD (verbatim) ===

PRODUCT: "Standup" — a shared daily-standup log for a small team.

PROBLEM. A six-person distributed team posts standups in chat, where they scroll away. Nobody can answer "what did Dana say she was blocked on last Tuesday?" without scrolling back through a week of unrelated messages. They want a durable record, addressable by day.

USERS. Team members, all equal. There is no admin role in v1.

SCREENS (three).
1. SIGN IN. Email and password. There is no sign-up screen in v1; accounts are seeded. Wrong credentials keep the user on this screen with an inline error.
2. TODAY. The current day's entries from everyone, newest first, each showing author email, timestamp, and the three fields. A composer at the top for the signed-in user's own entry. If they have already posted today the composer is pre-filled with their entry, and saving UPDATES it rather than adding a second one.
3. HISTORY. Pick a date, see that day's entries, read-only.

DATA. Exactly one PostgreSQL table, standup_entry:
  id            uuid        primary key
  author_email  text        not null
  entry_date    date        not null
  yesterday     text        not null
  today         text        not null
  blockers      text        null
  created_at    timestamptz not null
  updated_at    timestamptz not null
  UNIQUE (author_email, entry_date)
The uniqueness is a database constraint, not only an application check.

API. One REST resource, /api/entries.
  GET /api/entries?date=YYYY-MM-DD  -> that day's entries.
  PUT /api/entries                  -> upsert the signed-in user's entry for today; body carries yesterday, today, blockers.
Both require a session.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — these are what must read VERIFIED.
A1. Signing in with seeded valid credentials reaches TODAY.
A2. Signing in with a wrong password stays on SIGN IN and shows an error whose text is IDENTICAL to the error for an unknown email. The screen must not reveal whether an account exists.
A3. An unauthenticated GET /api/entries returns 401. It must not return an empty list.
A4. PUT /api/entries twice in one day for one user leaves exactly ONE row for that (author_email, entry_date), and the second body wins.
A5. The uniqueness in A4 holds AT THE DATABASE LEVEL: a direct second INSERT for the same (author_email, entry_date), bypassing the API, is rejected by the constraint.
A6. GET /api/entries?date=not-a-date returns 400 with a stable error code. Not a 500, and not a silent fallback to today.
A7. HISTORY for a date with no entries renders an explicit empty state. Not a blank screen and not a permanent spinner.
A8. blockers is optional. An entry saved with blockers empty round-trips and renders without a Blockers heading.

OUT OF SCOPE for v1: sign-up, password reset, editing another person's entry, deleting entries, notifications, a mobile layout, and any timezone other than UTC.

=== END PRD (verbatim) ===

KNOWN OPEN QUESTIONS I am deliberately leaving in, because a real PRD has them and manufacturing a fake ambiguity for Gate 1 to "find" would be exactly the circularity the governor's constraint (2) forbids: (a) HOW accounts are seeded is unspecified; (b) how far back HISTORY may reach is unspecified; (c) the PRD says entries are keyed by date and out-of-scope says UTC only, but does not say which clock decides "today" for the composer. If Gate 1 asks about none of these, that is a FINDING to record under DoD 1, not a step to fake.
